metadata.title: AI Semantic Reference
metadata.subtitle: Semantic contract for AI agents, retrieval systems, generators, validators, and advanced readers.
metadata.purpose: A public semantic contract for consistent Atlas terminology, boundaries, ownership, precedence, applicability, and verification status.

precedence.rule: A dedicated canonical registry has precedence over a cross-reference record.
The Formula registry owns formula expressions and verification status.
The Roles registry owns public role definitions; the Process Role Map owns contextual process assignments and authority boundaries.
Artifact definitions own structure and state; the Artifact Role Map owns contextual creation, custody, review, approval, verification, acceptance, and receipt assignments.
Lifecycle definitions own sequence, handoffs, and lifecycle context.
Decision Guides own scenario-specific action and escalation paths.
Shared semantic records define cross-cutting terminology and interpretation.
Current verified source material has precedence over Atlas synthesis.
Source-limited or synthesized material must be labeled as such.
When authority varies by organization, do not invent a universal rule.

recommended: Follow canonical links for full explanations.
Distinguish official source material from Atlas synthesis.
State uncertainty when a record is source-limited.
Do not infer that missing applicability means prohibition.
Do not treat commercial templates as PMI-prescribed forms.
Do not treat process groups as sequential lifecycle phases.
Do not equate waterfall with every form of predictive delivery.
Do not equate Scrum or Kanban with all adaptive delivery.
avoid: Stating earned value as merely a percentage.
Describing all hybrid work as a separate standardized framework.
Presenting Atlas-generated crosswalks as official PMI mappings.

concepts.concise_definition: A typical input, output, update, technique, or process dependency verified to an exact locator in the current official predictive supplement.
concepts.scope: The canonical relationship registry owns direction, action, applicability, source class, and locator; process and artifact pages are derived views.
distinctions: It is predictive reference scaffolding, not the July 2026 ECO hierarchy, a lifecycle phase model, or proof of mandatory linear sequence.
Typical does not mean required on every project; processes can overlap and repeat, and artifacts can be combined.

ai_guidance.use_when: Explaining or navigating a process input, output, update, technique, or dependency.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not turn the relationship into a mandatory lifecycle sequence or ECO hierarchy.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Name the relationship action, applicability, exact source status, and tailoring boundary.

concepts.concise_definition: A source-supported information or artifact relationship that a predictive process may consume, create, produce, or update when applicable.
concepts.scope: Creates, produces, and updates remain distinct lifecycle actions; raw work performance data, analyzed information, and reports remain distinct states.
distinctions: An update is not automatically a new artifact, and a listed output need not be a separate document.
A relationship does not transfer approval, staffing, procurement, or acceptance authority.
Verification establishes conformance evidence; acceptance records the designated acceptance authority's decision.
Work performance data, information, and reports are successive analytical forms rather than synonyms.
Inputs, outputs, updates, tools and techniques, direct dependencies, and supported transitions are complete across all 49 processes for the registered supplemental guide.

ai_guidance.use_when: Distinguishing what a predictive process may consume, create, produce, or update.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not reverse direction or collapse creates and updates.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: State the artifact, direction, lifecycle action, applicability, and relevant process.

concepts.concise_definition: The limit on interpreting predictive relationship data as universally required, separately documented, linear, or authority-conferring.
concepts.scope: Apply relationship detail in proportion to project context, delivery approach, governance, organizational policy, and delegated authority.
distinctions: Process Groups are interacting management-purpose groupings, not lifecycle phases.
The project manager coordinates within delegated authority and does not universally control organizational resources or contracts.
concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Atlas boundary derived from source caveats, current governance decisions, and the separation of relationship evidence from organizational authority.

ai_guidance.use_when: Preventing a process relationship from being overstated as mandatory, linear, separately documented, or authority-conferring.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not infer universal staffing, procurement, baseline, acceptance, or release authority.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Present the typical relationship, then state the relevant tailoring and authority limitation.

concepts.concise_definition: A working assessment that compares each stakeholder identifier's current and desired engagement state so the team can identify gaps and tailor engagement actions.
concepts.scope: The matrix uses Unaware, Resistant, Neutral, Supportive, and Leading states with C for current, D for desired, and C/D when the states are the same; identifiers should replace personal names where assessment information is sensitive.
distinctions: The matrix assesses engagement state; the Stakeholder Register owns stakeholder identity, influence, authority, and broader profile information.
The matrix informs the Stakeholder Engagement Plan but is not the plan itself.
The matrix may inform communication choices but is not the Communications Management Plan.
A power-interest or similar stakeholder grid classifies influence or interest; it does not show current-versus-desired engagement.
The matrix is a working assessment tool and is not asserted as a formal process output.
concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Lesson 3 supports the five-state current-versus-desired model; the extended evidence, action, owner, and review fields are clearly identified as an Atlas working-resource design.

ai_guidance.use_when: Comparing observed stakeholder engagement with the engagement needed for project success or explaining the resulting engagement gap.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not expose sensitive personal assessments, substitute the matrix for its related registers or plans, or present it as a required formal output in every delivery approach.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Define the five states and C/D markers, explain the gap, then distinguish the matrix from the register, engagement plan, communications plan, and influence-interest grids.

concepts.concise_definition: Champions the initiative and connects it to authorization, funding, strategic direction, and escalation authority.
concepts.scope: Commonly associated with authorization, strategic alignment, funding sponsorship, and decisions beyond delegated project authority.
distinctions: The sponsor is not automatically the customer, acceptance authority, operational owner, or benefits owner.
Specific approval rights come from the organization's governance model.
does_not_mean: Universal owner of every project decision

related_decision_guides.title: A Stakeholder Requests a Baseline Change
Transition or Closure Is Requested with Unresolved Obligations
Expected Benefits Are Not Yet Realized at Project Closure

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Exact sponsor authority varies by organization and initiative governance.

ai_guidance.use_when: Identifying authorization, strategic direction, funding sponsorship, or an escalation destination.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not assign the sponsor every approval or post-project ownership duty.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: State the commonly associated purpose, then qualify the exact authority as governance-dependent.

concepts.concise_definition: Integrates project work, information, and decisions within delegated authority.
concepts.scope: Commonly coordinates planning, execution, monitoring, communication, and escalation across the project system.
distinctions: Integration responsibility does not automatically grant specialist, sponsor, procurement, compliance, or acceptance authority.
Matters outside delegated limits are escalated through the governing route.

related_decision_guides.title: A Stakeholder Requests a Baseline Change
A Risk Occurs or an Impediment Exceeds Team Authority
Transition or Closure Is Requested with Unresolved Obligations

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: The extent of project-manager decision rights depends on delegated governance.

ai_guidance.use_when: Explaining integration, coordination, analysis, routing, and escalation.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not infer unrestricted authority from the role title.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Describe integration responsibility and name the authority boundary relevant to the scenario.

concepts.concise_definition: Performs and coordinates project work, contributes estimates and evidence, and resolves matters within team authority.
concepts.scope: Commonly owns execution details, collaboration, learning, and evidence produced by the work.
distinctions: Self-management may shape how work is performed without removing external governance or acceptance limits.

related_decision_guides.title: A Deliverable Fails Quality Inspection
A Risk Occurs or an Impediment Exceeds Team Authority

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Team composition and decision rights are tailored to the delivery and governance model.

ai_guidance.use_when: Explaining who performs work, estimates, collaborates, or removes team-level constraints.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not treat self-management as unlimited organizational authority.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: State the team's work purpose and separate team authority from external decision rights.

concepts.concise_definition: In product-oriented adaptive contexts, orders value-focused work and makes product decisions within the governing model.
concepts.scope: Most precise as a Scrum accountability; other adaptive approaches may use different product roles.
distinctions: Product prioritization is separate from technical verification and formal acceptance unless governance explicitly combines them.
does_not_mean: Generic name for every adaptive leader

related_decision_guides.title: A Risk Occurs or an Impediment Exceeds Team Authority
A Verified Deliverable Is Rejected During Acceptance

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Product-role naming and authority vary outside Scrum and across organizations.

ai_guidance.use_when: A Scrum or product-oriented context explicitly assigns value ordering or product decisions.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not generalize the accountability to all adaptive delivery or formal acceptance.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Name the framework or governance context before describing product-owner authority.

concepts.concise_definition: Formally accepts verified deliverables or scope results under the applicable agreement or governance model.
concepts.scope: Commonly associated with the decision that completed, verified results satisfy agreed acceptance criteria.
distinctions: Technical verification and formal acceptance are separate states and decisions.

related_decision_guides.title: A Verified Deliverable Is Rejected During Acceptance
Transition or Closure Is Requested with Unresolved Obligations

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: The accepting party and evidence required depend on governance and agreements.

ai_guidance.use_when: Explaining formal acceptance after technical verification.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not collapse verification into acceptance or invent the accepting role.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Identify the verified state, acceptance criteria, and governance-designated decision maker.

concepts.concise_definition: Provides organizational direction and decisions under the initiative's governance model.
concepts.scope: May decide funding, continuation, exceptions, baselines, escalation, or closure when those rights are explicitly assigned.
distinctions: Its mandate is defined by organizational governance rather than by a universal Atlas rule.
does_not_mean: A required committee with identical powers in every organization

related_decision_guides.title: A Stakeholder Requests a Baseline Change
A Compliance Problem Is Discovered
Transition or Closure Is Requested with Unresolved Obligations

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Governance structures and mandates are organization-specific.

ai_guidance.use_when: A decision exceeds delegated project, team, or specialist authority.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not assume a committee exists or assign it unstated powers.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Refer to the designated governance route and qualify its authority as organization-specific.

concepts.concise_definition: Evaluates and disposes controlled changes within an approved mandate.
concepts.scope: Commonly decides changes that affect controlled commitments, baselines, or other governance thresholds.
distinctions: A standing CCB is one governance design; change authority may be assigned differently.
does_not_mean: Required review body for every adaptive reprioritization

related_decision_guides.title: A Stakeholder Requests a Baseline Change
A Compliance Problem Is Discovered

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Thresholds and decision rights are defined by the governing change-control model.

ai_guidance.use_when: A proposed action may alter a controlled baseline or commitment.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not require CCB review for every work-level adjustment.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Identify the controlled commitment, threshold, and designated change authority.

concepts.concise_definition: Accepts operational responsibility for transferred outputs, support, controls, and residual obligations.
concepts.scope: Commonly associated with transition readiness and continuing operation after handoff.
distinctions: Operational ownership is distinct from formal project closure and benefits ownership.

related_decision_guides.title: Transition or Closure Is Requested with Unresolved Obligations
Expected Benefits Are Not Yet Realized at Project Closure

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: The receiving organization and its authority are organization-specific.

ai_guidance.use_when: Explaining transition, operational readiness, or post-transfer support responsibility.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not assume operations also owns every intended benefit.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Name the receiving role, transferred responsibilities, evidence, and unresolved obligations.

concepts.concise_definition: Owns defined benefit measures, dependencies, reviews, and continuing action after explicit handoff.
concepts.scope: Commonly associated with measurement and action after outputs transition into use.
distinctions: The project manager does not universally retain this role after formal closure.
does_not_mean: A universal authority model prescribed by the Atlas

related_decision_guides.title: Expected Benefits Are Not Yet Realized at Project Closure

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Post-project benefits authority depends on the organizational operating model.

ai_guidance.use_when: Explaining who continues measurement after project closure.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not assign continuing benefits ownership to the project manager by default.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Identify the explicit owner, measures, dates, dependencies, and escalation route.

concepts.concise_definition: Determines or advises whether defined quality criteria and verification requirements are satisfied within an assigned mandate.
concepts.scope: May be advisory, performing, approving, or auditing depending on the quality system.
distinctions: Technical verification does not itself create formal customer acceptance.

related_decision_guides.title: A Deliverable Fails Quality Inspection
A Verified Deliverable Is Rejected During Acceptance
A Compliance Problem Is Discovered

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: The quality role's mandate depends on the organization's quality system.

ai_guidance.use_when: Explaining technical criteria, inspection, testing, or verification decisions.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not equate verification authority with formal acceptance authority.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: State the quality decision and then identify any separate acceptance or change decision.

concepts.concise_definition: Owns or decides risk action, acceptance, escalation, or reporting within an assigned risk-governance mandate.
concepts.scope: May include individual risk owners, project risk leadership, or governance-level risk decision makers.
distinctions: Risk ownership and authority to accept exposure may be assigned to different roles.
does_not_mean: One universal role for every risk decision

related_decision_guides.title: A Risk Occurs or an Impediment Exceeds Team Authority
A Compliance Problem Is Discovered

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Risk thresholds, ownership, and acceptance authority vary by governance model.

ai_guidance.use_when: Explaining risk ownership, escalation, response, or exposure acceptance.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not assume the named risk owner can accept every level of exposure.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Separate action ownership from the authority to accept or escalate exposure.

concepts.concise_definition: Determines the sufficiency of compliance evidence or routes exception decisions within the applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, and organizational environment.
concepts.scope: Authority may be internal, external, advisory, approving, auditing, or controlling.
distinctions: Compliance obligations can affect scope
risk
quality
procurement
acceptance
transition
and closure.
does_not_mean: Universal permission to waive an obligation

related_decision_guides.title: A Compliance Problem Is Discovered
Transition or Closure Is Requested with Unresolved Obligations

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Exact authority comes from the obligation and governing environment.

ai_guidance.use_when: An obligation, evidence gap, exception, release, or stop-work decision is involved.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not invent an exception right or treat compliance as optional quality guidance.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Trace the obligation and evidence, then name the designated decision or escalation route.

concepts.concise_definition: Exercises sourcing, agreement, remedy, change, or closure rights within an assigned commercial mandate.
concepts.scope: Commonly associated with procurement strategy, source selection, agreements, seller administration, and commercial closure.
distinctions: The project manager integrates project impacts but does not automatically hold commercial authority.

related_decision_guides.title: Seller Performance Threatens Project Objectives
A Compliance Problem Is Discovered
Transition or Closure Is Requested with Unresolved Obligations

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Commercial decision rights depend on agreements and organizational delegation.

ai_guidance.use_when: A sourcing, agreement, remedy, seller, or commercial closure decision is involved.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not assign contract rights to the project manager without evidence.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Identify the agreement right, commercial mandate, and project-impact coordination required.

concepts.concise_definition: A delivery approach that establishes a comparatively broad authorized plan and baselines when work can be usefully defined in advance.
concepts.scope: Planning and control are tailored; prediction does not eliminate iteration, learning, or change.
distinctions: Predictive is a delivery approach
not a claim that the future is perfectly known.
concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: The concise contrast is an Atlas synthesis of the registered delivery-approach source set.

ai_guidance.use_when: Work can be planned comparatively broadly and governed through authorized plans or baselines.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not describe predictive delivery as non-iterative or immune to change.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Describe the planning horizon, control model, and tailoring context.

concepts.concise_definition: A familiar explanatory label for a comparatively sequential form of predictive delivery.
concepts.scope: Useful as a plain-language label when sequence and phase completion are emphasized.
distinctions: Waterfall is related to predictive delivery but is not a synonym for every predictive implementation.
concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: The registered sources support predictive terminology more directly than the informal waterfall label.

ai_guidance.use_when: A source or user explicitly uses waterfall to describe sequential predictive delivery.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not substitute waterfall for every predictive approach.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Treat waterfall as a familiar related label and prefer predictive for the broader category.

concepts.concise_definition: A delivery approach using short planning and delivery horizons with frequent review when learning and change are expected.
concepts.scope: Includes multiple frameworks and methods; form, cadence, roles, and artifacts vary.
distinctions: Adaptive is broader than Scrum or Kanban.
concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Cross-approach process applicability is Atlas synthesis, not an official PMI agile crosswalk.

ai_guidance.use_when: Learning, feedback, and changing priorities call for short planning and delivery horizons.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not infer one mandatory framework or remove governance constraints.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Describe the feedback cadence and tailored roles, artifacts, and controls.

concepts.concise_definition: A broad family of values, principles, and practices associated with adaptive and iterative delivery.
concepts.scope: Use as a broad orientation unless a specific framework or method is named.
distinctions: Agile is not interchangeable with Scrum
Kanban
or every adaptive implementation.
concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: The term is used broadly; specific claims require a named framework or method source.

ai_guidance.use_when: Referring broadly to adaptive values and practices without asserting a specific framework mechanic.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not attribute Scrum- or Kanban-specific rules to all agile work.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Use the broad term, then name the specific approach when mechanics matter.

concepts.concise_definition: A delivery approach that deliberately combines cadences or governance models and defines how their evidence and decisions reconnect.
concepts.scope: May combine adaptive product delivery with predictive funding, milestones, contracts, compliance, transition, or governance.
distinctions: Hybrid is a delivery approach
not a separate standardized set of 49 PMI processes.
concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Atlas mappings describe management-purpose applicability and are not official PMI framework crosswalks.

ai_guidance.use_when: Different components or governance levels intentionally use different cadences or controls.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not present hybrid as one standardized framework or a second process set.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Name the combined approaches and explain how evidence, authority, and decisions reconnect.

concepts.concise_definition: Refers to accountabilities, events, artifacts, or rules specific to Scrum; the informal phrase Agile ceremonies often means Scrum events but is not a universal agile meeting set.
concepts.scope: Use only when the framework context is explicit and the claim is actually Scrum-specific.
distinctions: Scrum is one framework within the broader adaptive landscape.
Scrum defines events; backlog refinement is ongoing activity rather than a formal event.
concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Framework-specific mechanics should be verified against an applicable Scrum source before being asserted.

ai_guidance.use_when: The framework is explicitly Scrum and the concept is one of its defined mechanics.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not generalize Scrum accountabilities, events, or artifacts to all adaptive delivery.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Label the statement Scrum-specific and separate it from broader adaptive guidance.

concepts.concise_definition: Refers to flow-oriented practices such as visualization, work-in-progress control, pull, and flow measures in a Kanban context.
concepts.scope: Use when the method or practice context is explicit.
distinctions: Kanban is not a synonym for every visual board or every adaptive approach.
concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Method-specific mechanics require an applicable Kanban source before being asserted.

ai_guidance.use_when: Flow, pull, WIP limits, or Kanban measures are explicitly in scope.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not label every board or adaptive practice Kanban.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Name the flow practice and keep it distinct from broader adaptive terminology.

concepts.concise_definition: The management purpose remains broadly applicable even when form, cadence, ownership, or storage changes.
concepts.scope: An Atlas applicability label used to describe a persistent management need across delivery approaches.
distinctions: Missing applicability means insufficient mapping
not prohibition.
concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Applicability mappings are an Atlas synthesis where the sources do not provide an official PMI agile crosswalk.

ai_guidance.use_when: The underlying management purpose persists across approaches with tailored implementation.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not imply identical artifacts, roles, cadence, or storage.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: State the common purpose and then describe how implementation may vary.

concepts.concise_definition: Estimated work fully completed by one team during one iteration in that team's chosen estimation unit.
concepts.scope: Concise semantic entry only; the Adaptive Metrics registry owns calculation, examples, and misuse boundaries.
distinctions: Only Done work counts.
Team-specific story points are not hours or comparable across teams.

ai_guidance.use_when: Same-team iteration forecasting is in scope.
ai_guidance.avoid: Never compare teams or count unfinished work.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Define the team and iteration and link to the canonical metric page.

concepts.concise_definition: The exact count of work items finished per unit of time.
concepts.scope: Canonical mechanics and example remain in the Adaptive Metrics registry.
distinctions: Counts items rather than story points.
The time period must be stated.

ai_guidance.use_when: Finished-item flow rate is in scope.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not omit the time unit.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: State the item count and observation period.

concepts.concise_definition: Elapsed time from when a work item started until it finished.
concepts.scope: Requires explicit workflow start and finish points.
distinctions: Includes active work and waiting inside the measured workflow.
does_not_mean: Lead time with an earlier request start

ai_guidance.use_when: Flow elapsed time is discussed.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not compare undefined endpoints.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Name the workflow start and finish.

concepts.concise_definition: Elapsed time from a defined request, order, or commitment point until delivery.
concepts.scope: The selected start and finish points must be stated; the Adaptive Metrics registry separately owns customer, commitment, procurement, and schedule-lead distinctions.
distinctions: May include waiting before active work.
It is at least cycle time only when the finish is shared and its start is earlier.
Predictive schedule lead is a precedence adjustment rather than this elapsed metric.

ai_guidance.use_when: Customer commitment or procurement responsiveness is discussed.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not leave boundaries implicit or confuse elapsed lead time with schedule lead.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: State start finish and time convention.

concepts.concise_definition: A chart of work remaining over time.
concepts.scope: Canonical chart mechanics and shared example data remain in the Adaptive Metrics registry.
distinctions: Scope additions can make the remaining-work line rise.

ai_guidance.use_when: Remaining work over time is discussed.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not hide changing total scope.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Name the work unit horizon and scope convention.

concepts.concise_definition: A chart of completed work increasing toward a separately displayed total-scope line.
concepts.scope: Canonical chart mechanics and shared example data remain in the Adaptive Metrics registry.
distinctions: A separate scope line makes scope change explicit.

ai_guidance.use_when: Completed work and total scope are plotted together.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not omit the total-scope series.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Distinguish completed work from current total scope.

concepts.concise_definition: A stacked view of cumulative work-item counts in workflow states over time.
concepts.scope: Canonical interpretation and example remain in the Adaptive Metrics registry.
distinctions: Band thickness represents inventory in a state.
A widening band can signal accumulation.

ai_guidance.use_when: Workflow-state accumulation over time is discussed.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not infer causation from one diagram.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Name the state band and the observed pattern.

concepts.concise_definition: A highly visible and current display of information useful to a team and stakeholders.
concepts.scope: A category of visual management rather than one required chart type.
distinctions: It should support conversation and action.
Digital displays can serve distributed teams.

ai_guidance.use_when: Highly visible current team information is discussed.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not define it as one chart type.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Name audience currency and intended action.

concepts.concise_definition: An uncertain event or condition that can affect objectives.
concepts.scope: Tracked while uncertainty remains and analyzed, owned, responded to, and monitored according to the risk approach.
distinctions: A realized risk may become an issue; not every issue began as a risk.
does_not_mean: A current problem already requiring corrective action

related_decision_guides.title: A Risk Occurs or an Impediment Exceeds Team Authority

ai_guidance.use_when: The event or condition is still uncertain.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not keep describing an occurred condition only as uncertain.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: State the uncertainty, objective effect, owner, response, and monitoring route.

concepts.concise_definition: A current condition requiring action, ownership, and possibly escalation or change.
concepts.scope: Captures current problems, decisions, or conditions that need resolution and traceability.
distinctions: A realized risk may create an issue
but not every issue began as a risk.

related_decision_guides.title: A Risk Occurs or an Impediment Exceeds Team Authority
A Compliance Problem Is Discovered

ai_guidance.use_when: A present condition requires action or a decision.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not require every issue to have originated as a registered risk.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: State the current condition, owner, action, due route, and escalation threshold.

concepts.concise_definition: Something currently blocking or slowing work.
concepts.scope: May be removed within team authority or tracked through issue management when broader action or traceability is required.
distinctions: Impediment terminology is not exclusive to Scrum.

related_decision_guides.title: A Risk Occurs or an Impediment Exceeds Team Authority

ai_guidance.use_when: Something presently blocks or slows work.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not restrict the term to Scrum or treat every impediment as a baseline change.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: State the constraint, owner, removal path, and when it becomes a broader issue.

concepts.concise_definition: A cross-cutting evidence chain connecting an obligation to implementation, verification, acceptance, transition, and closure records.
concepts.scope: Obligation or requirement → scope and acceptance criteria → risk and planning → quality and test evidence → procurement or agreement obligation where relevant → verification → acceptance → transition and closure evidence.
distinctions: Compliance is not one isolated process.
Exact authority depends on the regulatory, contractual, and organizational environment.

related_decision_guides.title: A Compliance Problem Is Discovered
Transition or Closure Is Requested with Unresolved Obligations

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: The chain organizes registered evidence without claiming one universal compliance method.

ai_guidance.use_when: Explaining how an obligation remains traceable through delivery and closure.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not isolate compliance in one process or invent authority to waive obligations.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Walk the obligation through criteria, plans, evidence, verification, acceptance, transition, and closure.

concepts.concise_definition: The explicit separation and connection among formal acceptance, transition, formal project closure, operational ownership, benefits ownership, and continuing benefits measurement.
concepts.scope: Formal acceptance confirms agreed results; transition transfers readiness and responsibility; formal closure completes project or phase obligations; operational and benefits owners continue assigned post-project responsibilities.
distinctions: Formal project closure may occur before all benefits are realized.
Continuing measurement requires an explicit handoff.
Operational ownership and benefits ownership may be assigned to different roles.
The Atlas does not assert a universal benefits-authority model.
does_not_mean: All benefits must be realized before closure
The project manager owns benefits indefinitely

related_decision_guides.title: Transition or Closure Is Requested with Unresolved Obligations
Expected Benefits Are Not Yet Realized at Project Closure

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: Post-project operational and benefits authority depends on the receiving organization.

ai_guidance.use_when: Explaining acceptance, transition, closure, or responsibility after project completion.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not delay closure until every benefit occurs or assign universal post-project ownership.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Separate each state and name the explicit operational and benefits handoffs.

concepts.concise_definition: A contextual judgment about which predictive, iterative, incremental, adaptive, or hybrid treatment fits the work and its components.
concepts.scope: Product, technical, people, stakeholder, governance, compliance, procurement, dependency, urgency, criticality, and organizational factors inform the decision without producing a universal score.
distinctions: Different components may use different treatments.
The Atlas factor map is not a PMI formula.
Predictive does not simply mean waterfall and adaptive does not mean Scrum.
concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: The decision aid organizes source-supported factors without copying or calculating the older guide's suitability questionnaire.

ai_guidance.use_when: Explaining why an approach fits a project or component.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not calculate a universal agile score or force one approach across every component.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Organize the factors by context then state treatment boundaries and authority.

concepts.concise_definition: A team that collectively has the capabilities needed to deliver value.
concepts.scope: Individuals may retain deep specialties; a generalizing specialist can add collaborative breadth without becoming a new Scrum accountability.
distinctions: Collective capability does not mean identical individual skill.
Specialists and shared authorities may remain.
Colocation and full dedication are contextual rather than mandatory.
does_not_mean: Generalizing specialist as a Scrum accountability

ai_guidance.use_when: Explaining adaptive team capability and topology.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not require every person to be a generalist or remove necessary specialist authority.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: Describe collective capability then make shared specialists and handoffs explicit.

concepts.concise_definition: Optional context-dependent practices such as spikes, pairing, swarming, continuous integration, automated testing, TDD, ATDD, and refactoring that can shorten feedback and reduce technical risk.
concepts.scope: These practices support delivery and quality but are not Scrum events or universal requirements.
distinctions: Continuous integration is not continuous deployment.
Automated tests do not replace all manual testing.
ATDD does not grant formal acceptance.
A spike has a question and time limit.

ai_guidance.use_when: Relating technical delivery practices to quality feedback and risk.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not make them Scrum events or equate automated acceptance checks with acceptance authority.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: State the purpose the optional boundary and the quality or authority connection.

concepts.concise_definition: A qualified procurement treatment that aligns commercial guardrails, acceptance, review, and change authority with iterative or incremental discovery and delivery.
concepts.scope: Fixed-scope, time-and-materials, staged, and hybrid structures allocate flexibility and risk differently; law and procurement policy control.
distinctions: No contract pattern is universal.
Product ordering does not alter an agreement.
Formal acceptance and contract-change authority remain explicit.

related_decision_guides.title: Seller Performance Threatens Project Objectives

concepts.atlas_synthesis_note: The comparison is instructional project-management guidance and does not recommend binding language or replace legal and procurement review.

ai_guidance.use_when: Explaining how procurement can accommodate iterative discovery.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not recommend a universal contract type or invent legal terms.
ai_guidance.answer_pattern: State what is fixed what may vary authority acceptance conditions and major risk.

concepts.concise_definition: The Formula registry is the canonical structured owner for formula expressions and verification status; this semantic reference only points to that owner.
concepts.scope: Formula and Quantitative Methods is the canonical public explanation for estimating, schedule, reserves, earned-value, and communication-channel formula families.
distinctions: Formula verification status must come from the Formula registry.
Shared semantics never independently assigns a formula-family verification status.
When records conflict, the Formula registry has precedence.

ai_guidance.use_when: Resolving where formula expressions, examples, or verification status are owned.
ai_guidance.avoid: Do not infer a formula's status from this semantic record or duplicate an expression here.
